content: DAW bridge/copilot architecture pattern (cross-DAW): every major DAW exposes an external-bridge seam via one of (a) an OSC bridge (Ableton LiveOSC/Max-for-Live, Bitwig DrivenByMoss OSC, FL Studio), (b) an embedded scripting API (Ableton remote scripts in Python, Reaper ReaScript in Lua/Python/EEL, FL Studio Python controller scripts), or (c) a plugin SDK (VST/AU hosting). Sonic Pi speaks OSC natively as its entire external interface. The dominant, battle-tested pattern: OSC for real-time event/control streaming (low-latency, lossy-tolerant), plus a higher-level scripting/IPC layer for reliable structured access. For an LLM-copilot that needs reliable bidirectional request/response with deterministic patch application and undo labelling, the consensus is a localhost TCP or stdio JSON-RPC/JSON-Lines channel over the Bitwig extension socket, with the in-DAW code kept a dumb mirror and the reasoning living outside. This matches Mario Zechner's 'what if you don't need MCP' argument: a tiny CLI with a short README (he cites ~225 tokens vs 13-18k for MCP servers) is composable across any agent/shell, which is exactly the bw-brain 'CLI is the stable contract' stance.
